trigger: concurrent delete_baseline landing between set_members/set_assignment's existence-check lease and its transaction lease, with an EMPTY member/assignment payload
independent_reporters: independently: 3 of 3 (cpp-safety organic Gate-3 discovery; unhappy-path UP-1 and consistency-auditor C1 same-wave Gate-4, blind to each other, given the lead as context but each did new independent analysis); echoed: 1 downstream (compliance-officer, PI1.1 framing)
summary: set_members/set_assignment's existence check and write transaction were two separate lease acquisitions; an empty payload skips the only statement (INSERT) that would hit the FK, so a row-count-blind touch-UPDATE could report success against a deleted baseline. consistency-auditor confirmed this is migration-introduced: the pre-migration SQLite store held one mutex across both operations. NOTE: severity as reported by 3 independent domain reviewers (SHOULD/MEDIUM); a strict I3(base HIGH)+E5(no change) rubric reading would derive HIGH - flagging this tension for the record rather than silently picking a label; practically moot since fixed regardless of exact band.

Only the deploy_baseline call site (the one this PR's diff touches) was fixed this round; update_baseline_from_form/delete_baseline_action are pre-existing untouched code, deferred.

trigger: a failed locker COMMIT inside the new race test's REQUIRE would unwind the stack while std::thread t was still joinable
independent_reporters: independently: 2 of 2 (quality-engineer and cpp-safety, both targeted round-3 re-reviews of the same new test, converged on the identical fix shape without seeing each other's report)
policy_floor: cpp-safety's own blocking-contract class (unjoined-thread-adjacent teardown hazard) per cpp-safety's severity_native call; classified MEDIUM by the orchestrator since the trigger (COMMIT failing on a bare DELETE+COMMIT with no prior errors) is near-impossible in practice, not because the hazard class itself is discounted
summary: Fixed proactively based on quality-engineer's report (before cpp-safety's independent confirmation landed): COMMIT result captured, t.join() called unconditionally, THEN REQUIRE asserts on the captured result - matches cpp-safety's independently-arrived-at recommended fix exactly. Also fixed quality-engineer's secondary note: call_start moved inside the thread lambda so the timing assertion can't silently pass on a late-scheduled thread that only reached the touch-UPDATE after COMMIT.
